task: Horizon 13: Breaking Changes in stage/prod are accepted through Git (ADR-0015 accepted-change records). Settle what a record holds, how an Environment knows it already applied one, whether records are ever removed, and what happens if the Source has drifted again by apply time. Also cover how a Breaking Change in a PR branch is handled unattended (the accept-schema --branch gap).

analysis.objective: Make a committed accepted-change record in the Project the only way a Breaking Change is accepted in stage, prod and unattended PR Branch Environments. Each record lists the accepted dropped or retyped columns of one Pipeline table. An Environment's next run applies the record at most once and tracks it by id in that Environment's own Warehouse. `adops accept-schema` (CLI and the dev-only MCP accept_schema tool) writes these records, and `adops validate` checks them. This is the ADR-0015 slice of the v1 vision's 'a Breaking Change halts the affected Step and downstream Steps' rule.
analysis.successDefinition: Done when ALL hold, with tests at 100% line and branch coverage on the adops package and the demo E2E green on Postgres and DuckDB. (1) An accepted-change record is a small plain YAML file pipelines/accepted/<id>.yaml (id = file name, so ids are unique by construction) holding a Pipeline name, a table name and a non-empty list of changes in BreakingChange.message wording ('<column> dropped' or '<column> retyped (<from> -> <to>)'), types normalized when matching. (2) adops validate reports a sanitized '<file>: ...' problem for bad YAML, an unknown Pipeline, a table no Sync Step of that Pipeline loads, an empty change list or a malformed change; record files are never read as Pipelines and never change Step Fingerprints. (3) In stage, prod and Branch Environments a Sync Step whose Breaking Changes are all covered by unapplied records relaxes NOT NULL on covered dropped columns, syncs, and after every Check passes saves the new snapshot and the used record ids in one transaction; the Step result names each applied record. Any uncovered change halts the Step and downstream Steps naming only the uncovered changes and telling the user to add an accepted-change record to the PR; nothing is applied. (4) Applied record ids live in _adops_applied_records in each Environment's own adops schema (br_<branch>__adops for a Branch); a stored id never applies again there. dev never applies records. (5) The demo E2E shows stage halting on a Breaking Change, passing once a covering record file is added, and not applying it again on the next run. (6) No code path deletes record files; a Breaking Change is never accepted automatically; GLOSSARY describes accepted-change records. accept-schema writing records, --env stage|prod becoming read-only, --branch and the ADR-0015/0014 text are the next horizon.
assumptions: confirmed: record content is the list of accepted changes for one Pipeline table
confirmed: uncovered Breaking Change at apply time halts the Step and applies nothing
confirmed: applied record ids are tracked per Environment in its own Warehouse; at most once per Environment
confirmed: dev accept-schema (CLI or MCP) writes the record from dev's view; hand-written YAML is the fallback, checked by adops validate
confirmed: Branch Environments apply records like stage; accept-schema --branch added; halt message says to add a record to the PR
confirmed: record files are kept forever
confirmed: accept-schema --env stage|prod writes a record file, never that Warehouse
The record id is the record file's name, unique across the Project; accept-schema names it <UTC timestamp>-<pipeline>-<table>.
Records live in a subfolder under pipelines/ (e.g. pipelines/accepted/), inside the MCP edit_file boundary and outside the top-level pipelines/*.yaml Pipeline glob.
A change is matched exactly: same column, same kind and, for a retype, the same normalized from/to types. A record may list more changes than an Environment sees.
A record is marked applied only on a run where it covered at least one Breaking Change found there and the Step's Checks passed.
Several unapplied records for the same table may together cover one run's Breaking Changes; every record that covered at least one is marked applied.
Applying happens inside the existing whole-Warehouse lock (one lock per Warehouse; a Branch run holds stage's), in the same run that saves the snapshot.
dev never applies records, because dev accepts by hand.
Server scheduled runs and the merge/release workflows already see committed records via the updated Server Project folder (horizon 8).
The applied-records table is created when first needed, like _adops_schema_snapshots; drop-branch CASCADE removes it with the branch.
risks: Step Fingerprints hash Project files; if record files under pipelines/ count toward a Sync Step's fingerprint, adding a record makes branches rebuild or re-sync. The choice must be deliberate.
An unapplied record stays pending forever; if the same column change later appears in that Environment, the old record silently accepts it.
Saving the snapshot and the applied ids must be ordered so a crash never leaves a record marked applied without the new snapshot (or the reverse); DuckDB and Postgres differ.
Branch baselines start fresh (horizon 6), so a Branch may never see the change the record was written for, giving a false sense it was tested before merge.
Supersession: horizon-2 decision 'accepted only via adops accept-schema --env' must be superseded in decisions.md and in tests asserting --env stage writes the Warehouse.
Horizon-10 'MCP accept_schema is dev only' stays for Warehouse writes; writing the record from MCP must not widen the tool to stage/prod names (ADR-0009).
Type strings must match through normalize_column_type; validate should normalize hand-written types so 'int4' and 'integer' match.
MCP edit_file has no special handling for record files; validate errors and the halt message must be enough to fix a bad record without Warehouse access.
accept-schema --env stage|prod changes from a Warehouse write to a file write; the CLI output must say nothing was applied yet and the file must be committed.
outOfScope: An 'Accept' button on the Dagster page or any other unreviewed acceptance — ADR-0015 rejected it.
The Assistant committing, pushing or opening the PR that carries a record — the MCP server does no Git (horizon-9 decision); the six skills are a later horizon.
Removing, archiving or expiring record files — kept forever by user decision.
Accepting added columns or a full new TableShape — records list only dropped or retyped changes.
Copying stage's snapshots or applied ids into a new Branch Environment — branch baselines start fresh (horizon 6).
Automatic drop-branch on PR merge or close — stays manual (horizon 6).
New Breaking Change kinds (renames, NOT NULL tightening) — find_breaking_changes keeps dropped and retyped.
Changing the Server's Git update flow or Promotion workflows — horizon 8 already delivers the checkout.
Changing the MCP allow-list or adding stage/prod MCP tools — ADR-0009 stays.
A cross-Environment 'pending records' report — not needed to unblock unattended runs.
analysis.domainShapeReason: The objective is a DataOps governance rule — who may accept a Breaking Change in which Environment, reviewed through Git, and when it is applied or halted — across real seams between Pipeline schema rules, Environments and the Assistant interface.

ubiquitousLanguage.meaning: A dropped or retyped column in a Source table compared with the Environment's saved schema snapshot; it halts the Sync Step and its downstream Steps unless accepted.
A committed YAML file in the Project (ADR-0015) with a unique id, one Pipeline table and the list of accepted Breaking Changes.
What a stage, prod or Branch run does when unapplied records cover every Breaking Change found: continue the Step, save the new snapshot and store the record ids as applied.
The small table in each Environment's adops schema, next to _adops_schema_snapshots, holding ids of records that Environment applied.
A Breaking Change no unapplied record lists exactly; any uncovered change halts the Step and only those are named.
The adops command and dev-only MCP tool: in dev it accepts in dev's Warehouse and writes a record; with --env stage|prod it only writes a record; with --branch it writes the Branch snapshot by hand.
dev, stage, prod or a Branch Environment (br_<branch>__ schemas in stage's Warehouse); each keeps its own snapshots and applied records.
The accepted TableShape of a Pipeline table in adops._adops_schema_snapshots of one Environment's Warehouse, saved only after every Check of the Step passes.

discoveryFindings.finding: PlannedStep.__call__ runs preflight, then preflight Checks, then builds shapes, then calls _raise_if_breaking(shapes) BEFORE sync.sync. _raise_if_breaking loads previous via snapshot_store.load(warehouse, pipeline, step.source, table), calls find_breaking_changes, collects a dict table->changes and raises BreakingChangeError(step, breaking). Message: 'Step <s>: Breaking Change in <table>: <c1.message>, ...; ...'. run_step turns it into StepStatus.FAILED and InOrderOrchestrator skips later Steps.
discoveryFindings.implication: Record coverage belongs in _raise_if_breaking: subtract changes covered by unapplied records, raise BreakingChangeError only with uncovered ones, and add 'add an accepted-change record to the PR' text. Do it before any NOT NULL relaxation or sync, so nothing is applied on a halt.

discoveryFindings.finding: After the load and declared Checks pass (_raise_if_failed), PlannedStep calls self._save_shapes(shapes). That calls snapshot_store.save once per table, each in its own guarded call and its own connection/transaction. There is no 'used records' state anywhere. PlannedStep fields are step, source, warehouse, pipeline, snapshot_store, clock. It has no Environment name and no records.
discoveryFindings.implication: PlannedStep (built in _build_plan) needs new fields: the records that apply (empty for dev) plus an applied-records store, or a combined port. _save_shapes must save the snapshot and the applied ids together, and the NOT NULL relaxation (sync.make_columns_nullable) must run between the coverage check and sync.sync.

discoveryFindings.finding: run_pipeline(pipeline_text, settings_text, environment_name, env, sync, snapshot_store, clock, orchestrator, transform, reverse_sync, fingerprinting, branch) takes text and ports only. It reads no files. The dev/stage/prod/branch decision is environment_name plus the optional BranchRun.
discoveryFindings.implication: Records must reach run_pipeline as parsed domain objects, or as texts through a port like ProjectFiles. Add a keyword parameter that defaults to none so the many existing tests keep working. Apply records only when the Environment is not 'dev' (domain/assistant_access.DEV, or a new domain predicate).

discoveryFindings.finding: Protocol with load(warehouse, pipeline, source, table) -> TableShape|None and save(warehouse, pipeline, source, table, shape). Its docstring says it keeps the shape and never judges a change. FakeSnapshotStore is in tests/unit/application/fakes.py:208.
discoveryFindings.implication: To add applied ids, extend the port (e.g. applied_ids(warehouse, pipeline, table) and save(..., applied_ids=())) or add a sibling port. Either way the fake in fakes.py and every place that builds a store must be updated. Keep 100% branch coverage (guard g2).

discoveryFindings.finding: Each call opens a dlt pipeline 'adops_schema_snapshots' with dataset_name=layout.adops ('adops' or 'br_<branch>__adops'), passing branch_schemas=layout!=default so '__' is not normalized. It creates the dataset and runs CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS _adops_schema_snapshots(pipeline, source, table_name, shape_json, recorded_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now) on every use. There is no primary key. save is DELETE then INSERT inside client.begin_transaction(). The same SQL serves Postgres and DuckDB through the dlt sql_client.
discoveryFindings.implication: An _adops_applied_records(record_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, pipeline, table_name, applied_at) table fits in the same _client() CREATE block. The DELETE/INSERT of the snapshot and the INSERT of the ids can share the one begin_transaction(), which works for both DuckDB and Postgres. A multi-table Step still saves table by table, so save per table with that table's record ids.

discoveryFindings.area: 2. per-Environment adops schema and local state
discoveryFindings.finding: build_snapshot_store(project, environment, kind, layout) builds WarehouseSnapshotStore. Its local dlt state is in .adops/dlt/<environment>. A Branch run passes layout=SchemaLayout.for_branch(name) (adops schema 'br_<branch>__adops') and the Branch Environment name. Stage, prod and dev use 'adops' in their own Warehouse.
discoveryFindings.implication: Applied ids are kept per Environment automatically if they live in the same store. drop-branch already runs DROP SCHEMA ... CASCADE on br_ schemas (infrastructure/warehouse_schemas.py:65), so a Branch's applied table is removed with the branch.

discoveryFindings.finding: The analysis assumes a per-Pipeline Warehouse lock. warehouse_lock is one exclusive lock per Warehouse: a fixed Postgres ADVISORY_LOCK_KEY, or fcntl for DuckDB. A Branch run takes stage's lock (_holding_lock(project, STAGE, ...)). accept_schema (CLI and MCP) takes no lock at all (horizon-10 decision).
discoveryFindings.implication: Applying records happens inside run_in_environment/_run_branch's whole-Warehouse lock, which is fine. accept-schema --branch writing into stage's Warehouse should decide whether to take stage's lock, as drop-branch does.

discoveryFindings.finding: accept_schema(pipeline_text, settings_text, environment_name, table, env, sync, snapshot_store) -> AcceptedSchema(pipeline, environment, step, table, shape, nullable_columns). It preflights one table, loads previous, takes the DROPPED columns from find_breaking_changes, calls sync.make_columns_nullable, then snapshot_store.save. It never returns the list of BreakingChange. It uses pick_environment, not stage_environment.
discoveryFindings.implication: Return the found changes (the full tuple, not only dropped) in AcceptedSchema so the dev path can write the record. Pull the dropped-column relaxation out into a shared function that run_pipeline's apply path also uses. Add a branch variant that uses stage settings and the Branch layout.

discoveryFindings.finding:
Arguments are pipeline and table. Options are --env (default 'dev') and --project. There is no --branch. Output: 'Accepted the current shape of ( columns, Step ) for Pipeline

in Environment .' plus the nullable line. accept_project_schema reads the files and builds the sync and store through run_command factories. Errors go through fail().
discoveryFindings.implication: Add a --branch option that refuses --env, as run does in run_command.py:241. Resolve it via stage_branch_name and SchemaLayout.for_branch. Branch the stage/prod path to write a record file and print a 'commit it' message. Write record files from the interface layer (filesystem), not from application.

discoveryFindings.area: 3. tests asserting --env stage writes the Warehouse
discoveryFindings.finding: test_accept_schema_in_stage_uses_stage_local_state_and_finds_stage_snapshot (line 317) asserts that --env stage builds the store with .adops/dlt/stage and makes stage_only nullable. test_env_option_targets_only_that_environment (line 154) and test_adapters_are_built_for_the_chosen_environments_kind (line 268, parametrized env/kind) also cover non-dev envs.
discoveryFindings.implication: These tests must be rewritten as part of the supersession: --env stage/prod writes only a record and builds no store. Supersede decisions.md horizon-2 line 10 and the horizon-6 'accept-schema --branch is a known gap' line 39.

discoveryFindings.finding: accept_schema(pipeline, table, environment=None, branch=None). It runs plain_pipeline_name, then guarded_run_arguments (allows only dev or a branch, and refuses a dev that shares the stage/prod DB), then refuse_branch_schema_acceptance(branch), which raises ACCEPT_SCHEMA_DEV_ONLY. It then calls accept_project_schema(project, name, table, DEV) and replies AcceptedSchemaReply(pipeline, table, step, environment, column_count, nullable_columns).
discoveryFindings.implication: Keep the dev-only guard (ADR-0009). Write the record from the shared interface function that the CLI also uses. Add a record path/id field to AcceptedSchemaReply, plus a 'no Breaking Change seen' reply. Tests at test_mcp_server.py:1044-1142 assert the arguments and refusal texts.

discoveryFindings.finding: allowed_project_path(write=True) requires parts[0] in PROJECT_FILE_ROOTS=('pipelines','dbt') and len(parts)>=2. It refuses '..', .env* and absolute paths. write_project_file creates missing parent folders (mkdir parents=True), so pipelines/accepted/x.yaml is writable and listable.
discoveryFindings.implication: present: hand-written records through MCP edit_file need no change to the boundary. The record writer for accept-schema can reuse write_project_file or plain Path writes in the interface layer.

discoveryFindings.finding: run_command.pipeline_files = sorted((project/'pipelines').glob('*.yaml')), which is non-recursive. Users: run --all, mcp load_pipelines/project_view, server._pipelines. validate_command._pipeline_files uses its own identical glob('*.yaml'). There is no rglob over pipelines/. ProjectTree.read_tree is rglob but is used only for dbt Transform folders.
discoveryFindings.implication: A pipelines/accepted/ subfolder is never read as a Pipeline. Records should use a separate glob, e.g. pipelines/accepted/*.yaml, through a new shared helper. A unit test should pin that pipeline_files ignores subfolders.

discoveryFindings.area: conflict: Pipeline-name path vs record folder
discoveryFindings.finding: Pipelines are addressed as pipelines/<name>.yaml (read_project_files). A Pipeline whose name is 'accepted' would be pipelines/accepted.yaml, which can sit next to the pipelines/accepted/ folder without conflict. On case-insensitive filesystems that is still no clash.
discoveryFindings.implication: No blocker. The folder name should be a module constant in one place, shared by validate, run and accept-schema.

discoveryFindings.area: 6. Step Fingerprint of a Sync Step
discoveryFindings.finding: current_fingerprints uses step_fingerprint(canonical_step_json(step), _step_files(step)). _step_files returns project_files.read_tree(step.project) only for a TransformStep and {} otherwise. A Sync Step's fingerprint is its canonical JSON alone, and a Transform hashes only its dbt project folder.
discoveryFindings.implication: Adding a record file under pipelines/accepted/ does not change any fingerprint and forces no branch re-sync. The plan must state this choice and pin it with a test. The risk is that a PR that only adds a record leaves its Branch fully deferred, so the record is never exercised in the Branch.

discoveryFindings.finding: _run_branch_locked builds plan_branch_run from stage's fingerprints and uses layout=SchemaLayout.for_branch(name) for sync and snapshot store, with stage settings. run_pipeline returns all-DEFERRED when first_changed is None. Otherwise _build_plan builds only steps[first:], so deferred Sync Steps never preflight or check for Breaking Changes.
discoveryFindings.implication: Records are consulted in a Branch only for rebuilt Sync Steps. The Branch snapshot starts empty (load returns None), so its first run never sees a Breaking Change. A Branch halts only when the Source changes between two Branch runs of a rebuilt Sync Step.

discoveryFindings.finding: The Branch Environment name is stage_branch_name(stage, branch), which goes through branch_environment_name with a hash suffix when the name is too long. It sizes the name to stage's longest Source name. The schema prefix is drop_prefix(name) = '<name>__'.
discoveryFindings.implication: accept-schema --branch must derive the name exactly this way, with stage settings and stage's Warehouse, so it writes the same br_<x>__adops schema that runs read.

discoveryFindings.finding: validate_project(project, pipeline) builds a Report(problems, skipped, schedules). It loads adops.yaml, then each pipeline file via _load(project, relative, loader, report), which prefixes problems with the relative path and handles a missing file or non-UTF-8 text. It then runs _check_connections and _check_dbt_projects. The MCP validate tool returns the same report.
discoveryFindings.implication: Add a _check_records(project, loaded pipelines, report) step after the pipeline loop. Reuse _load with a new domain load_record so bad YAML gives the same sanitized '<file>: ...' lines. Check ids against file names, duplicates, unknown Pipeline, a table no Sync Step loads, an empty list and malformed changes. Decide whether validate <pipeline> checks only that Pipeline's records.

discoveryFindings.finding: Server load_definitions raises ServerConfigError when validate_project(project, None).problems is non-empty. The pull-request, stage and prod workflow templates all run 'adops validate' before 'adops run --all'.
discoveryFindings.implication: A malformed record will stop the Server from loading and fail the workflows. This is intended (fail early), but error text must name the file and stay sanitized. Record checks must not need a Warehouse.

discoveryFindings.finding: BreakingChange(column, kind: BreakingChangeKind{DROPPED,RETYPED}, previous_type, current_type=None) is a frozen dataclass. message gives '<col> dropped' or '<col> retyped (<from> -> <to>)', with parentheses. normalize_column_type lowercases, maps aliases and keeps parameters and [] depth. find_breaking_changes skips _dlt_ columns and sorts.
discoveryFindings.implication: A record change can be parsed into BreakingChange. A DROPPED record has no previous_type, so matching must compare only (column, kind) for dropped, and (column, kind, normalize(from), normalize(to)) for retyped. The record text form '<col> retyped <from> -> <to>' differs from .message (parens): choose one format and parse it in the domain.

discoveryFindings.area: 9. loader conventions for a new file kind
discoveryFindings.finding: load_pipeline and load_project_settings use _load(model, text): yaml.safe_load must give a mapping, then pydantic model_validate. Errors become PipelineValidationError lines '<path>: msg' via format_path, with include_input=False so values are never echoed, and nothing is chained. Validators can raise RuleViolation for multi-problem detail.
discoveryFindings.implication: Add a domain AcceptedChangeRecord pydantic model (pipeline, table, changes: list[str] parsed into BreakingChange) and load_accepted_record(text) built on _load. The domain must stay framework-free apart from pydantic/yaml, which it already uses (guard g5, test_domain_purity).

discoveryFindings.finding: tests/unit mirrors the layers: domain/, application/ (fakes.py holds FakeSnapshotStore and fake fingerprint stores), infrastructure/ (test_schema_snapshot_store.py uses real DuckDB files, and Postgres through ADOPS_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN in CI), and interface/ (mcp_harness.py, test_accept_schema_command.py, test_validate_command.py, test_run_command.py). Domain and application have purity tests.
discoveryFindings.implication: Each phase adds tests in the matching folder. The applied-records adapter needs DuckDB tests and Postgres-DSN tests, including a transaction rollback test for the atomic snapshot+ids save.

discoveryFindings.finding: test_demo_incremental_breaking_change_and_missing_table runs dev, then ALTER TABLE orders DROP COLUMN customer_id in the shop Source and asserts 'Breaking Change in orders: customer_id dropped' plus skipped downstream Steps. It then runs 'accept-schema shop_sync orders' (dev) and asserts 'in Environment dev.' and 'may now be NULL ... customer_id', then re-runs. The demo fixture is parametrized over postgres and duckdb, and the shop() helper runs SQL against the Source.
discoveryFindings.implication: Extend this test, or add one: also run stage before the ALTER, check that stage halts and names the change, run dev accept-schema to write the record, and check that stage passes on the next run and does not re-apply the record on a second run. The new assertions on dev output (record file path) must be added.

discoveryFindings.finding: In the demo adops.yaml, dev and stage share the same shop Source DB (port 15432, database shop) and use separate Warehouses (warehouse vs warehouse_stage, or separate DuckDB files). warehouse(demo, sql, environment=...) can query stage. One ALTER is therefore seen by both dev and stage.
discoveryFindings.implication: A stage record-apply E2E needs no new Source fixture: one ALTER drives both Environments. reseed_shop restores the Source. The e2e job has a 20-minute timeout across both params (guard g4), so add steps to the existing scenario rather than a new full-demo test.

discoveryFindings.finding: The GLOSSARY has 'Breaking Change' (it halts the whole Sync Step and later Steps 'until resolved'). There is no entry for accept-schema, accepted-change record, schema snapshot or applied records.
discoveryFindings.implication: Add 'Accepted-change record' (with _Avoid_ terms) and update Breaking Change to say how it is resolved per Environment. Follow the glossary's bold-term, definition, _Avoid_ format.

discoveryFindings.finding: ADR-0015 says the Assistant opens a PR adding an accepted-change record, a human merges, the Server pulls, and the next run records the new shape. Consequences: accept-schema 'produc[es] a record in the Project that each Environment applies on its next run; running it by hand stays available for dev and Branch Environments.' ADR-0014 line 15 points Git acceptance to horizon 8.
discoveryFindings.implication: Update the Consequences with what was built: record location and format, applied ids per Environment Warehouse, uncovered-change halt, --env stage|prod writes only a record, --branch, records kept forever. Also fix the stale horizon-8 pointer in ADR-0014.

discoveryFindings.finding: The CI step greps an explicit list of demo/plain/server/github template files in the wheel. init_command._copy_tree copies template directories recursively (iterdir). The demo has only pipelines/shop_sync.yaml, and plain has no pipelines/ folder.
discoveryFindings.implication: No template folder is needed: accept-schema creates pipelines/accepted/ on first write (mkdir parents). If a pipelines/accepted/.gitkeep template is added, list 'pipelines/accepted/.gitkeep' in the demo loop, check that hatch ships dotfiles, and update test_init_command.

discoveryFindings.finding: Coverage must be 100% line and branch on src/adops, with only TYPE_CHECKING excluded.
discoveryFindings.implication: Each new branch needs a unit test: covered/uncovered/partial records, multiple records, already-applied ids, dev skips, the atomic save failing, the validate error kinds, the accept-schema dev-none-seen and --branch cases, and the MCP record reply.

discoveryFindings.area: guard g5: layering and no pragma
discoveryFindings.finding: The domain/application purity tests forbid framework imports, and 'pragma: no cover' is banned apart from TYPE_CHECKING.
discoveryFindings.implication: Record parsing and coverage matching go in the domain (pure). Reading record files from disk and writing them go in interface or infrastructure. run_pipeline gets records as values or through a port.

discoveryFindings.finding: ruff check runs E,F,W,I,B,UP with line-length 100.
discoveryFindings.implication: New code follows the existing 100-column style.

discoveryFindings.finding: pytest tests/e2e -m e2e runs on ubuntu with Docker, with a 20-minute job timeout. The demo fixture runs every scenario twice (postgres and duckdb).
discoveryFindings.implication: Keep the added E2E steps minimal (a few extra adops runs) so the job stays within 20 minutes.

discoveryFindings.finding: Server load_definitions finds Pipelines with pipeline_files. Each scheduled run calls run_in_environment(project, pipeline, environment, InOrderOrchestrator()), the same function adops run --env uses. It reads the Project files at call time, so committed records pulled by horizon 8 are seen.
discoveryFindings.implication: Load records inside run_in_environment and _run_branch_locked, not in the CLI wrapper, so the Server, run --all, MCP run (run_project) and the workflows all apply records through one seam.

discoveryFindings.finding: present: _adops_schema_snapshots is created lazily in <layout>.adops per Environment.
discoveryFindings.implication: Create the applied-records table in the same lazy CREATE IF NOT EXISTS block.

discoveryFindings.area: needs: dropped-column NOT NULL relaxation via Sync port
discoveryFindings.finding: present: Sync.make_columns_nullable(step, table, warehouse, columns) is implemented in DltSync, and accept_schema uses it.
discoveryFindings.implication: Reuse it in PlannedStep for covered DROPPED changes, per table, before sync.sync.

discoveryFindings.area: needs: Server reads the updated Project from Git (horizon 8)
discoveryFindings.finding: unknown: no Git pull code is in src. The Server reads the bind-mounted Project folder at call time, and the stage/prod workflows run validate and run on the self-hosted runner after checkout. ADR-0014 still says Git acceptance comes 'with horizon 8'.

discoveryFindings.area: needs: MCP accept_schema has no Warehouse lock / dev only
discoveryFindings.finding: present: horizon-10 decision line 73 says MCP accept_schema is dev only and takes no lock, and refuse_branch_schema_acceptance enforces it.
discoveryFindings.implication: The MCP stays dev-only. --branch is CLI-only unless the user decides otherwise. Update the ACCEPT_SCHEMA_DEV_ONLY text if 'nothing to accept there' becomes untrue.

uv run pytest tests/unit --cov with fail_under=100 line+branch on src/adops; only 'if TYPE_CHECKING:' excluded
builds the wheel and greps for an explicit list of template files; a new template file not added to the list is not checked, a listed file missing fails CI

phases.name: Add the accepted change record and coverage rule
phases.goal: Add a pure domain type for an accepted-change record. It parses from plain YAML, writes back to YAML, and has one rule that splits the Breaking Changes a run found into the ones unapplied records cover and the ones they do not.
phases.rationale: Every later phase depends on one shared definition of a record: the run that applies it, the validate check, and the accept-schema command that writes it. Keeping the parsing and matching pure, with no I/O, lets all three use the same rule and test it without a Warehouse. dump_accepted_record has no caller in this horizon; it is built here because the very next horizon's accept-schema writes records with it, and the round-trip test is what keeps record files and the halt text in the same wording.
changes: Create a frozen AcceptedChangeRecord(id, pipeline, table, changes: tuple[BreakingChange, ...]). The id is the record file's name without '.yaml' and is passed in by the caller.

Add load_accepted_record(record_id, text) built on the existing loader._load pattern: yaml.safe_load must give a mapping with 'pipeline', 'table' and a non-empty 'changes' list of strings. Errors are PipelineValidationError lines that never echo values (include_input=False, nothing chained).

Add parse_change(text) that reads exactly the BreakingChange.message wording: '<column> dropped' or '<column> retyped (<from> -> <to>)'. Normalize both types with normalize_column_type. Raise a clear RuleViolation for any other shape.
Add dump_accepted_record(record) that writes the same YAML, changes in BreakingChange.message wording, so dump then load gives the same record back.

phases.name: Change Sync Steps to apply accepted-change records
phases.goal: In stage, prod and Branch Environments, a Sync Step that finds Breaking Changes continues when unapplied records cover all of them. It relaxes NOT NULL on the covered dropped columns, syncs, and after every Check passes saves the new snapshot together with the ids of the records it used. Any uncovered change halts the Step as today, names only the uncovered changes, and applies nothing.
phases.rationale: Records are how stage, prod and unattended PR Branch runs get past a Breaking Change without anyone at a terminal, so the run itself has to act on them. The rule goes where Breaking Changes are detected today (PlannedStep._raise_if_breaking), before any write, so a halt still changes nothing.
changes: Extend the SchemaSnapshotStore port with applied_record_ids(warehouse) -> frozenset[str]. Add a keyword applied_record_ids: Sequence[str] = () to save(), with the contract that the snapshot and the ids are stored atomically. Update FakeSnapshotStore to match.

Add a keyword-only records: Sequence[AcceptedChangeRecord] = () parameter to run_pipeline. Keep only records whose pipeline matches, and use none when environment_name is dev (dev accepts by hand). Pass the records for each table into PlannedStep through _build_plan.

In PlannedStep._raise_if_breaking, call snapshot_store.applied_record_ids only when the table has records, then call cover(). Raise BreakingChangeError with only the uncovered changes. Outside dev, add the text 'add an accepted-change record for <table> to the PR' to the message (the folder name stays only in the interface constant).
Pull the dropped-column relaxation into one shared application function. Call it for covered DROPPED columns via sync.make_columns_nullable per table, after the coverage check and before sync.sync.

In _save_shapes, pass each table's used record ids to snapshot_store.save only when that table used records, so a run with no records calls save exactly as today and the real WarehouseSnapshotStore (extended in the next phase) keeps working; ids are stored only after every Check passed.
Add one line per applied record to the Step result text (e.g. 'Applied accepted-change record <id> in <env>'), so the CLI output and Run Log name every record a run applied.
phases.expectedResult: run_pipeline applies records through PlannedStep. Unit tests with FakeSnapshotStore show: a covered change passes and stores the used ids, an uncovered change halts naming only that change with nothing saved or relaxed, an already-applied record is ignored, failed Checks store no ids, and dev ignores records, and the Step result names each applied record.

g2: every new branch (no records, covered, partial, applied, dev, failed checks) has a test; the default records=() keeps existing tests unchanged

phases.name: Add an applied records table to snapshot storage
phases.goal: WarehouseSnapshotStore keeps applied record ids in a new _adops_applied_records table next to _adops_schema_snapshots in each Environment's adops schema. It writes them in the same transaction as the snapshot.
phases.rationale: Each Environment must remember in its own Warehouse which records it already applied, so a record applies at most once there. Writing the ids and the snapshot in one transaction means a crash can never leave one saved without the other.
changes: In the existing lazy CREATE block in _client(), also run CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS _adops_applied_records(record_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, pipeline TEXT, table_name TEXT, applied_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()).

Test on real DuckDB files and on Postgres through ADOPS_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN: round trip, the Branch layout (br_<branch>__adops) is kept separate from 'adops', and a failing id insert rolls back the snapshot.

phases.healerHint: The most likely failure is a lost or non-atomic id write: the INSERT sits outside begin_transaction, or the snapshot DELETE also clears the ids. rubric.label: A Pipeline argument limits record cross-checks
rubric.ruleStatement: When validate is given one Pipeline, it skips the pipeline and table cross-checks for records of other Pipelines. It still reports parse errors in every record file. The MCP validate tool shows the same problems.
passCriteria: A test runs validate_project(project, pipeline='a') with a record for an unloaded Pipeline 'b' and asserts no 'unknown Pipeline' problem for it
The same setup with a malformed record for 'b' still reports the parse problem for that file (parse errors are reported for every record file regardless of the Pipeline argument)
A test or existing shared-report path asserts the MCP validate tool output includes a record problem: `uv run pytest tests/unit -k "mcp and validate"` passes
failureExamples: 'adops validate a' reports every other Pipeline's record as 'unknown Pipeline', because only 'a' was loaded
The MCP validate tool builds its own report and does not show record problems

phases.healerHint: The most likely failure is a scoped validate run reporting false 'unknown Pipeline' errors, or a table check that accepts any table name. Fix it by cross-checking only records whose pipeline is in the loaded set, and by comparing against the tables of that Pipeline's Sync Steps.

successCriteria: Done when ALL hold, with tests at 100% line and branch coverage on the adops package and the demo E2E green on Postgres and DuckDB. (1) An accepted-change record is a small plain YAML file pipelines/accepted/<id>.yaml (id = file name, so ids are unique by construction) holding a Pipeline name, a table name and a non-empty list of changes in BreakingChange.message wording ('<column> dropped' or '<column> retyped (<from> -> <to>)'), types normalized when matching. (2) adops validate reports a sanitized '<file>: ...' problem for bad YAML, an unknown Pipeline, a table no Sync Step of that Pipeline loads, an empty change list or a malformed change; record files are never read as Pipelines and never change Step Fingerprints. (3) In stage, prod and Branch Environments a Sync Step whose Breaking Changes are all covered by unapplied records relaxes NOT NULL on covered dropped columns, syncs, and after every Check passes saves the new snapshot and the used record ids in one transaction; the Step result names each applied record. Any uncovered change halts the Step and downstream Steps naming only the uncovered changes and telling the user to add an accepted-change record to the PR; nothing is applied. (4) Applied record ids live in _adops_applied_records in each Environment's own adops schema (br_<branch>__adops for a Branch); a stored id never applies again there. dev never applies records. (5) The demo E2E shows stage halting on a Breaking Change, passing once a covering record file is added, and not applying it again on the next run. (6) No code path deletes record files; a Breaking Change is never accepted automatically; GLOSSARY describes accepted-change records. accept-schema writing records, --env stage|prod becoming read-only, --branch and the ADR-0015/0014 text are the next horizon.
